chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Barnet alumni, Bill Harris and Flip Phillips join the First Herd
summary: Ralph Burns, Chubby Jackson and Frances Wayne came from Charlie Barnet's band; he then found Bill Harris and Flip Phillips.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: How did he get on the band? Did you recruit him?

No, as a matter of fact, there was a whole contingent -- well, not that many, a couple-three came directly from the Charlie Barnet band. I didn't know that they had been with Charlie until much later. But Ralph was with
Charlie's band and so was Chubby, and so was Francis Lane. Wayne.

And -- but I think they felt that they would be able to express themselves a little more fully, coming with us, and that's what happened. That was a transition period, and that's when we -- then I started to look for people and found people like Bill Harris and -- who'd been in a few bands, but no one had really utilized him. And from there, -- as a matter of fact, he had just done the Benny Goodman -- the a picture with Benny Goodman, prior to joining me. And I think that was probably the first time he was really -- where he had a chance to play anything.

And then Flip Phillips came in the band. I got him from Russ Wes Morgan's band in New York. And he stayed with the band about a month, and then he got worried because he figured that Russ Wes Morgan was a much more working band, and that his success -- and he would be able to call his shots and be able to keep everybody happy, working.

So he left the band, and then about a month later, we were starting to get some -- we were around the Paramount Theatre for ten weeks at a crack or something, and all of a sudden, Flip was ready to rejoin. But he was always very skeptical, and I think that proved it.
